cause: Categorical expansion compared a same-named persisted indicator against the server-derived contrast before reusing it, but polynomial expansion refused any same-named column on name alone, so composing a second workflow on a dataset already carrying a derived power failed before fitting.

evidence.ref: bash scripts/gate.sh --full: backend 4245 passed, golden 23 no drift, frontend 1508, tsc clean

impact: A persisted power column is now reused only after proving it is the requested term: identical missing-value positions, and finite values equal within a 1e-9 relative tolerance that admits a serialization round trip while refusing any difference of analytical consequence. The stored values are kept rather than rewritten, so a durable column stays byte-identical across compositions, and a non-matching same-named column still fails closed. Golden 23 held with no drift, confirming the shared term-expansion path changed no existing estimate. This is the condition that made a live acceptance run fail with experience_pow2 collides after an earlier workflow had created that column.
lesson: Two derived-term families sharing one expansion module must share its reuse semantics; comparing values for one and names for the other turns a legitimate recomposition into a pre-fit failure.
